title: Siddhartha Sees the World
bigQuestion: What did the prince see outside the palace, and why did it make him ask why?

story.title: Outside the Palace Gate
story.kicker: A prince rides out and sees something new.
paragraphs: Buddhists tell this story. Long ago, a prince named Siddhartha lived in a big palace. He had gardens, music and good food. His father wanted him to be happy every day.
One day the prince rode out of the palace gate. His driver was named Channa. On the road, the prince saw a man with white hair and a bent back. He walked slowly with a stick.
"Who is that?" the prince asked. "That is an old man," said Channa. "Everyone grows old one day." The prince was quiet. He had never seen an old person before.
That night the prince did not sleep well. He kept thinking. Why do people grow old? Why do people get hurt? He wanted to know.
story.think: What question would you ask if you saw something for the very first time?

lessons.title: A Prince Named Siddhartha
lessons.mainIdea: Buddhists tell of a prince named Siddhartha who lived long ago in India.
reading: Buddhists tell a story about a boy named Siddhartha. He lived about 2,500 years ago. His home was in the north of India, near Nepal today.
His father was a king. His mother was a queen named Maya. Siddhartha was a prince. He would grow up to be called the Buddha.

words.d: the son of a king and queen

look.title: Picture the Palace
look.text: Look at a big palace with tall walls. Inside are green gardens and a pond with flowers. A boy sits by the pond. He has everything he could want.
look.prompt: What would you like to see if you lived in this palace?

check.why: The Buddhist story says Siddhartha was a prince, the son of a king.
The story takes place in northern India about 2,500 years ago.
Buddhists tell that Queen Maya was his mother. Channa was his driver.

lessons.title: Walls All Around
lessons.mainIdea: The story says the king kept sad things away from his son.
reading: The king loved his son. The story says he wanted the prince to see only happy things. So the palace had high walls.
Inside the walls, no one was sick or old where the prince could see. Siddhartha did not know about sadness yet. Buddhists say he had never seen it.

words.d: a very big house where a king or queen lives

look.title: Only Happy Things
look.text: Look at the prince in his garden. Music plays. Flowers bloom. Every face he sees is smiling. Outside the wall, the town is busy with all kinds of people.
look.prompt: What might the prince not know about, if he only sees his garden?

check.q: Why did the palace have high walls?
check.why: The story says the king wanted his son to see only happy things.
Buddhists tell that he had never seen sadness inside the palace.

check.q: Who built the walls to keep sad things out?
check.why: The story says his father, the king, wanted to protect him.

lessons.title: A Sick Man and an Old Man
lessons.mainIdea: Outside the walls, the prince saw a sick man and an old man.
reading: Buddhists tell that the prince went outside the walls. First he saw a man who was very sick. Then he saw a man who was very old.
The prince was surprised. His driver said that all people can get sick. All people grow old. The prince felt sad for them.

words.d: not feeling well in your body

look.title: On the Road
look.text: Look at the dusty road. An old man walks with a stick. Nearby, a sick man rests by a tree. The prince stops his cart to look.
look.prompt: How do you think the prince felt? What face would he make?

check.q: What did the prince see first outside?
check.why: In the story he saw a sick man and an old man.

check.q: What did the driver tell him?
choices: all people can get sick and old
check.why: Channa said sickness and old age come to everyone.
The story says he felt sad and began to wonder.

lessons.title: A Funeral and a Calm Man
lessons.mainIdea: Next he saw a funeral, and then a calm holy man.
reading: Next the prince saw people carrying a man who had died. His family was crying. This was a funeral. The prince felt very sad.
Last, he saw a holy man in a plain robe. The man looked calm and peaceful. Buddhists call these four the Four Sights.

words.d: the sick man, old man, funeral and holy man the prince saw

look.title: The Four Sights
look.cite: Buddhist life stories of the Buddha, such as the Jataka's opening story (Nidanakatha)

check.q: What did the prince see last?
check.why: In the Four Sights, the calm holy man comes last.
Buddhists call them the Four Sights.

check.q: How did the holy man look?
check.why: The story says the holy man was calm, and this gave the prince an idea.

lessons.title: A Big Question
lessons.mainIdea: The prince wondered why people suffer.
reading: The prince kept thinking about what he saw. Why do people get sick? Why do they grow old? Why are people sad?
Buddhists say he wanted to find a way to help. He wanted to understand suffering. Suffering means hurting or feeling sad.

look.title: Wondering
look.text: Look at the prince sitting by his window at night. The moon is bright. He is not playing. He is thinking hard about the people he saw.
look.prompt: What is one big question you wonder about?

check.q: What did the prince want to know?
check.why: The story says the Four Sights made him ask why people suffer.
Suffer means to hurt or feel sad.
Buddhists say he wanted to find a way to help.

lessons.title: Leaving the Palace
lessons.mainIdea: Buddhists tell that the prince left the palace to find an answer.
reading: One night the prince made a hard choice. He left the palace. He left his fine clothes and his riches.
Buddhists tell that he wanted to find an answer to his question. He became a traveler looking for wisdom. His search had begun.

words.d: knowing what is true and good

look.title: Two Kinds of Asking
look.text: Some questions have quick answers, like "What is for lunch?" Some questions take a long time, like "Why are people sad?" The prince asked a long-time question.
look.prompt: Can you think of a quick question and a long-time question?

check.q: What did the prince leave behind?
check.why: The story says he left the palace and his riches to search.
Buddhists tell that he left to answer his question about suffering.

choices: knowing what is true and good
check.why: Wisdom means knowing what is true and good.

review.why: The story says Siddhartha was a prince, so his father was a king.
The Four Sights are the sick man, old man, funeral and holy man.

review.q: Which sight made the prince feel hopeful?
review.why: The calm holy man showed him a peaceful way to live.
The Four Sights led him to ask why people suffer.
This is the story Buddhists tell about the Buddha's life.

review.q: What did the prince do at the end?
review.why: He left the palace to search for an answer.
